info.title: EchoCall Developer Platform - High-Performance AI Voice & Chat API
info.description:
Welcome to the **EchoCall Public API**. This platform is designed for developers, resellers, and enterprises to programmatically build, manage, and scale ultra-realistic AI voice agents and smart chatbots.

### 🚀 Getting Started
Our API follows RESTful principles and returns standard JSON responses. To start building, you'll need:
1.  **An API Key**: Generate your `eck_live_...` key in the [EchoCall Developer Portal](https://hub.echocall.de/developer).
2.  **Base URL**: Use `https://hub.echocall.de/api/v1` for all requests.

### 🔐 Authentication & Security
EchoCall uses **Bearer Token Authentication**. Send your API key in the `Authorization` header:
```bash
curl -X GET "https://hub.echocall.de/api/v1/agents" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"
```
> [!IMPORTANT]
> Keep your keys secure. A key grants full access to your account's data under its scopes.

### 🧑‍💼 Acting on behalf of a customer
Reseller keys can run any customer-facing operation as one of their customers by adding the header `X-EchoCall-Customer: <customerId>`. The request is then treated exactly as if that customer had sent it: ownership, limits and usage are the customer's, and none of the reseller operations are reachable with the header set. This is how a self-hosted front end serves many customers with a single key. The customer id is the one returned by `POST /resellers/customers`.
```bash
curl -X GET "https://hub.echocall.de/api/v1/agents" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_RESELLER_KEY" \
     -H "X-EchoCall-Customer: 501"
```

### 🎭 White-labeling & Reselling
EchoCall is built with an **API-First White-labeling Strategy**. 
-   **Proprietary Models**: EchoCall utilizes its own high-performance models, `EchoCall-Voice` and `EchoCall-Smart`, specifically optimized for low-latency conversational AI.
-   **Reseller Scopes**: Resellers can manage their own customers via the `/resellers` endpoints, adjusting balances, credits, and plans dynamically.

### 🚦 Rate Limiting & Pagination
-   **Rate Limits**: Limits are applied **per API key, per second** (`rateLimitPerSecond`, **500 requests per second** by default). Every response carries `X-RateLimit-Limit` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining`. Exceeding the limit returns **429** with `Retry-After: 1`.
-   **Pagination**: Most list endpoints support `page` and `perPage` query parameters. `page` starts at 1; the default `perPage` varies per endpoint and the maximum `perPage` is **100**.

### 🔔 Webhooks
Register an endpoint with `POST /webhooks` and EchoCall pushes events to it as they happen. `GET /webhooks/events` returns the full catalog; subscribe to `"*"` to receive everything.

**Envelope.** Every delivery is a single JSON object:
```json
{
  "id": "evt_1f0c9a24-6f0e-4a1e-9f0c-2b6a1c1c1c1c",
  "event": "call.ended",
  "createdAt": "2026-01-31T09:12:44.512Z",
  "data": { }
}
```

**Headers.**
| Header | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `X-EchoCall-Event` | Event name, same value as `event` in the body. |
| `X-EchoCall-Delivery` | Envelope id. Use it to make your handler idempotent. |
| `X-EchoCall-Signature` | `t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>` (see below). |
| `User-Agent` | `EchoCall-Webhooks/1.0` |

**Signature verification.** `v1` is the HMAC-SHA256 of `${t}.${rawBody}`, keyed with the secret returned once when the webhook was created. Compute it over the **raw** request body, before any JSON parsing, and compare in constant time:
```js
import crypto from 'crypto';

function verify(secret, header, rawBody, toleranceSeconds = 300) {
  const parts = Object.fromEntries(header.split(',').map((p) => p.split('=')));
  if (Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - Number(parts.t)) > toleranceSeconds) return false;
  const expected = crypto.createHmac('sha256', secret).update(`${parts.t}.${rawBody}`).digest('hex');
  const a = Buffer.from(expected);
  const b = Buffer.from(parts.v1 ?? '');
  return a.length === b.length && crypto.timingSafeEqual(a, b);
}
```

**Delivery, retries and auto-disable.** Answer with any 2xx status within **10 seconds**; anything else counts as a failure. A failed delivery is retried three times, after **1s**, **5s** and **30s**. `lastDeliveryAt` and `lastDeliveryStatus` on the webhook record the final outcome of each event, `failedDeliveries` counts consecutive failures and resets to 0 on the next success. After **25** consecutive failures the endpoint is set to `isActive: false` and receives nothing until you re-enable it with `PATCH /webhooks/{id}`. Use `POST /webhooks/{id}/test` to check an endpoint at any time; that ping is sent once, with no retry.

> [!NOTE]

### Errors

Every failing request answers with the same envelope, whatever went wrong:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "validation_error",
    "message": "Invalid request body",
    "details": { "name": { "_errors": ["Required"] } }
  }
}
```

Branch on `error.code`, never on `error.message`: the code is stable, the wording is not.
`details` appears only on validation failures and carries the per-field report from the
request schema.

| Status | `error.code` | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation_error`, `invalid_id`, `invalid_date`, `bad_request` | The request could not be accepted as written. |
| 401 | `unauthorized`, `invalid_api_key` | The `Authorization` header was missing, malformed, or the key is unknown, revoked or expired. |
| 402 | `insufficient_balance` | The account wallet does not cover the purchase. |
| 403 | `insufficient_permissions`, `forbidden` | The key is valid but lacks the required scope, or the endpoint is reseller-only. |
| 404 | `not_found` | No such resource is visible to this key. Resources owned by another account are reported as missing. |
| 409 | `conflict` | The resource exists but its state does not allow the operation. |
| 412 | `provider_not_configured` | The account is not yet provisioned for the voice engine. |
| 429 | `rate_limit_exceeded` | Too many requests. Wait for `Retry-After` seconds. |
| 500 | `internal_error`, `database_error` | An unexpected server fault. Safe to retry. |
| 502 | `upstream_error`, `sync_failed` | A dependency the endpoint needs answered badly. |
| 503 | `service_unavailable`, `marketplace_disabled` | The feature is switched off for this deployment. |

A 403 caused by a missing scope also carries `error.requiredScope`, naming the scope the key
would need.

### Scopes

Every API key carries a set of scopes. Each operation names the one it requires in its
`x-required-scope` extension, and self-service keys are currently issued with all of them.
Reseller endpoints (`/resellers`) and the provisioning hooks (`/provisioning`) carry a scope like
every other operation, and additionally require the key to belong to a reseller account: the
scope alone does not make a key a partner key.

| Scope | What it allows |
| --- | --- |
| `read:agents` | Read voice agents, their knowledge sources and their integration assignments. Also required for the voice library and for reading batch calling campaigns. |
| `write:agents` | Create, change and delete voice agents, their knowledge and their integration assignments. Also required to create, submit, cancel and delete batch calling campaigns. |
| `read:chatbots` | Read chatbots, their knowledge sources and their integration assignments. |
| `write:chatbots` | Create, change and delete chatbots, their knowledge and their integration assignments. |
| `read:phone-numbers` | List owned numbers, browse the marketplace and read regulatory verification state. |
| `write:phone-numbers` | Buy, reassign, cancel numbers and submit regulatory verification documents. Purchases charge the account wallet. |
| `read:conversations` | Read call records, chat conversations and chat transcripts. |
| `write:conversations` | Send messages into a chat conversation, reassign it, archive it and close it. |
| `read:analytics` | Read usage, revenue and per-agent performance aggregates. |
| `read:webhooks` | List webhook endpoints and read the event catalog. |
| `write:webhooks` | Register, change, test and delete webhook endpoints. |
| `read:tickets` | Read support tickets and their message threads. |
| `write:tickets` | Open tickets and post replies. |
| `read:integrations` | List integrations, read one with its credentials masked, and read the tool catalog. |
| `write:integrations` | Connect, change, test and remove integrations. |
| `read:billing` | Read plans, invoices, subscription, wallet balance and transactions. |
| `write:billing` | Start a checkout for a plan. |
| `read:profile` | Read the account profile, its usage and limits, and the notification inbox. |
| `write:profile` | Mark notifications read. |
| `read:resellers` | Read partner data: customers, plans, subscriptions, invoices, analytics and settings. |
| `write:resellers` | Change partner data and run the provisioning lifecycle hooks. |

### Pagination

List endpoints take `page` (1-based) and `perPage`. `perPage` is clamped to at most 100
everywhere; the default differs per endpoint and is stated on each operation. The response
carries a `pagination` object with `page` and `perPage`, and with `total` only where the
handler runs a count query. Where `total` is absent, that is documented on the operation:
page until you receive fewer items than you asked for.

ApiKeyAuth.description: Send the API key as a bearer token: `Authorization: Bearer eck_live_...`. That is the only accepted form; the header must start with `Bearer ` exactly, and the token must match `eck_(live|test)_[a-f0-9]{64}`. Keys are issued in the Developer Portal and carry a set of scopes; each operation names the scope it needs in its `x-required-scope` extension.

ActAsCustomer.name: X-EchoCall-Customer
ActAsCustomer.description: Reseller keys only. Runs this request as the named customer of the reseller, exactly as if that customer had sent it with a key of their own: ownership checks, limits and usage all apply to the customer, and none of the reseller operations are reachable while it is set. The value is the customer id returned by `POST /resellers/customers` and listed by `GET /resellers/customers`. Errors: 400 `invalid_customer_header` (not a positive integer), 403 `act_as_requires_reseller` (not a reseller key), 404 `customer_not_found` (no customer of this reseller with that id), 403 `customer_suspended`. The `/resellers/*` and `/provisioning/*` operations never accept it.

post.description: Gives a voice agent access to one integration, so its tools become callable during a call. post.description: Buys one of the numbers returned by the search and attaches it to the account. This charges money: the setup price plus the first month, plus 19 percent VAT, is deducted from the account wallet, a balance transaction is written and an invoice is issued. Pass the listing from the search result back unchanged. Prices are never taken from the request: the server prices the number again from the marketplace listing, or from the platform price list for the countries that carry one, so the `setupPrice`, `monthlyPrice`, `providerSetupCost` and `providerMonthlyCost` fields are accepted for compatibility and ignored. Read the `pricing` block of the response for what was actually charged. A listing that can no longer be priced, because it has been withdrawn or its SKU has changed, is answered with 502 `quote_failed`: search again and retry with a current listing. If the wallet does not cover the total the request is rejected with 402 and nothing is bought. If the billing profile of the account is incomplete (company name, street, postal code, city, country, and the VAT ID for EU countries) the request is rejected with 412 `billing_profile_incomplete` before anything is charged, because the invoice could not be issued; complete the company details under Settings and retry. They remain in the schema only so integrations that echo a whole search result back keep working.

get.description: Returns every outbound webhook endpoint registered by the account, newest first and unpaged. The customer must belong to the calling reseller, otherwise the answer is also 404, so that one reseller cannot probe for another reseller customers. On success the owner is set and the purchase timestamp is stamped with the current time. A body that fails validation answers 400 with `error.code` set to `validation_error` and `error.message` carrying the raw list of validation issues as an array of objects, not as a human-readable string.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the phone number record to assign. A non-numeric value answers 400 `invalid_id`.

requestBody.description: The customer that shall receive the number, given by its numeric user id.

post.summary: Take a phone number back from a customer
post.description: Returns a number to the reseller inventory. The owner and the purchase timestamp are cleared, any pending cancellation is cleared as well, and a revocation timestamp is stamped. The number only has to be booked under the calling reseller: releasing a number that is already unassigned succeeds and simply rewrites the same empty state. A number belonging to another reseller, or none at all, answers 404. This endpoint takes no request body. The API key must belong to a reseller account.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the phone number record to release. A non-numeric value answers 400 `invalid_id`.

post.x-no-request-body: This endpoint takes no request body.

200.description: The number was released back into the inventory.

get.summary: Get usage totals for a date window
get.description: Aggregates everything the reseller customers consumed in a date window into a single set of totals, split into a chat share and a voice share, and reported both as revenue (what the reseller charged) and as base cost (what the platform charged the reseller). Without query parameters the window runs from the first day of the current month to now. Both bounds are inclusive of whatever the date parser makes of them. The response is the totals object itself, not wrapped in a `data` envelope. Only a reseller key reaches this route.

parameters.name: startDate
parameters.description: Start of the window, as an ISO 8601 date or date-time. Defaults to the first day of the current month, keeping the current time of day. A value the date parser cannot read answers 400 `invalid_date`.

parameters.name: endDate
parameters.description: End of the window, as an ISO 8601 date or date-time. Defaults to the moment the request is handled. A value the date parser cannot read answers 400 `invalid_date`.

200.description: Usage totals for the requested window.

totalChatSessions.description: Chat sessions billed in the window.

totalVoiceMinutes.description: Voice minutes billed in the window.

totalRevenue.description: What the reseller charged its customers in the window, in EUR.

totalBaseCost.description: What the platform charged the reseller for the same consumption, in EUR.

totalMargin.description: Revenue minus base cost, in EUR.

chatSessionRevenue.description: The chat share of `totalRevenue`, in EUR.

voiceMinuteRevenue.description: The voice share of `totalRevenue`, in EUR.

chatSessionCost.description: The chat share of `totalBaseCost`, in EUR.

voiceMinuteCost.description: The voice share of `totalBaseCost`, in EUR.

get.summary: Get the revenue and margin breakdown for a date window
get.description: Reads the same aggregation as the usage endpoint but reports it from the commercial side: total revenue, the platform share of it, the margin left to the reseller, and that margin as a percentage. The percentage is reported as 0 when there was no revenue in the window, so an empty period never produces a division by zero. Window defaults and date validation match the usage endpoint: first day of the current month to now, and 400 `invalid_date` for a value that cannot be parsed. A key from a non-reseller account is rejected with 403.

parameters.name: startDate
parameters.description: Start of the window, as an ISO 8601 date or date-time. Defaults to the first day of the current month, keeping the current time of day. A value the date parser cannot read answers 400 `invalid_date`.

parameters.name: endDate
parameters.description: End of the window, as an ISO 8601 date or date-time. Defaults to the moment the request is handled. A value the date parser cannot read answers 400 `invalid_date`.

200.description: The revenue breakdown for the requested window.

totalRevenue.description: What the reseller charged its customers in the window, in EUR.

platformRevenue.description: The part of that revenue the platform charged the reseller, in EUR.

resellerMargin.description: Revenue minus platform cost, in EUR.

marginPercent.description: The margin as a percentage of total revenue. 0 when there was no revenue.

get.summary: Get payment status and invoicing profile
get.description: Reports whether the reseller has payment credentials on file and returns the company data printed on invoices. No secret is ever returned: the stored card processor secret key and the stored wallet credentials are reduced to the booleans `stripeConfigured` and `paypalConfigured`. The publishable key is returned in full, because it is meant to be public. Company fields that were never filled in come back as empty strings rather than null. Answers 404 when the reseller record behind the key has disappeared. Reseller keys only.

patch.description: Writes the card processor and wallet credentials used to bill the reseller own customers. Every field is optional and only the fields you send are written, so this is a partial update. Empty strings are treated as absent and leave the stored value untouched, which means credentials cannot be cleared through this endpoint. The change is recorded in the reseller activity log as `payment_keys_updated`. Values written here are never readable again through the API. A body that fails validation answers 400 with `error.code` set to `validation_error` and `error.message` carrying the raw list of validation issues as an array of objects, not as a human-readable string. Requires a reseller-owned API key.

requestBody.description: The credentials to store. Send only the ones you want to change.

patch.description: Updates the company details that appear on invoices the reseller issues to its customers. All fields are optional and the object you send is written as given, so sending a field with an empty string does clear it, unlike the trading name, which must be at least one character when present. The email field must be a valid address. The change is recorded in the activity log as `company_data_updated`. A body that fails validation answers 400 with `error.code` set to `validation_error` and `error.message` carrying the raw list of validation issues as an array of objects, not as a human-readable string. The calling key has to belong to a reseller.

requestBody.description: The invoicing company fields to change.

get.summary: Get the company and branding profile
get.description: Returns the branding side of the reseller profile: trading name, legal name, address, VAT id, the logo used on invoices, the accent colour of the branded portal and the portal logo. Fields that were never set come back as null here, unlike the settings endpoint, which reports empty strings. Answers 404 if the reseller record cannot be loaded. Access is limited to reseller accounts.

patch.summary: Update the company and branding profile
patch.description: Partially updates the branding profile. Every field is optional and only the keys you send are written. The portal logo accepts null explicitly, which removes it, while the remaining fields take strings only. Note that the trading name, address and VAT id overlap with the invoicing profile written by PATCH /resellers/settings/company: both endpoints write the same stored record. The change is recorded in the activity log as `company_profile_updated`. A body that fails validation answers 400 with `error.code` set to `validation_error` and `error.message` carrying the raw list of validation issues as an array of objects, not as a human-readable string. Reseller keys only.

requestBody.description: The profile fields to change. Omitted fields keep their stored value.

get.summary: Get the balance with a warning level
get.description: Returns the reseller prepaid EUR balance together with a health classification meant for dashboard banners. The level is `healthy` at 5 EUR or more, `warning` from 1 EUR up to 5 EUR, and `critical` below 1 EUR, and `shouldShowBanner` is true whenever the balance is under 5 EUR. A preformatted string with a euro sign is included so a caller does not have to format it. Answers 404 when the reseller record behind the key no longer exists. Use GET /resellers/balance for the plain figure. A non-reseller key is refused with 403.

200.description: The balance and its warning level.

balance.description: Current prepaid balance in EUR, as a number.

shouldShowBanner.description: True when the balance is below 5 EUR.

formattedBalance.description: The balance rendered with a euro sign and two decimals.

get.description: Returns the audit entries written whenever a reseller action changes something: customer creation, pricing changes, credential updates, suspensions and the like. Entries come back newest first. The listing is capped rather than paginated: pass `limit` to change the page size, which defaults to 50 and is clamped into the range 1 to 200, with values above 200 reduced to 200. There is no offset, so older entries beyond the limit are not reachable through this endpoint. Reseller keys only.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many entries to return, newest first. Clamped into the range 1 to 200; a value that is not a number falls back to 50.

get.summary: List the voice agents of all customers
get.description: A read-only overview of every voice agent owned by any customer of the calling reseller, newest first, each paired with a short reference to its owner. The listing is not paginated and returns an empty `data` array when the reseller has no customers yet. Each entry nests the stored agent record under `agent`: this is the whole database row with the internal provider columns and credential columns removed, so it carries more fields than the summarised agent shape used elsewhere in this API. The endpoint is read-only; use the agent endpoints to change anything. The API key must belong to a reseller.

200.description: Every voice agent across the reseller customer base.

agent.description: The stored voice agent record. The handler selects the whole database row and then removes the internal provider columns and credential columns, so further stored columns beyond those listed here can appear.

id.description: Numeric identifier of the voice agent.

userId.description: The customer account that owns it.

resellerId.description: The reseller the record is booked under.

name.description: Internal name of the voice agent.

get.summary: List the chatbots of all customers
get.description: The chatbot counterpart of the voice agent overview: every chatbot owned by any customer of the calling reseller, newest first, each with its owner. Not paginated, and an empty `data` array when there are no customers. Each entry nests the stored chatbot record under `chatbot`, again as the whole database row minus the internal provider and credential columns. Read-only. Only a reseller-owned key is accepted, any other key is answered with 403.

200.description: Every chatbot across the reseller customer base.

chatbot.description: The stored chatbot record. The handler selects the whole database row and then removes the internal provider columns and credential columns, so further stored columns beyond those listed here can appear.

userId.description: The customer account that owns it.

resellerId.description: The reseller the record is booked under.

get.summary: Get platform prices, reseller prices and margins
get.description: Returns what the platform charges the reseller per chat session and per voice minute, what the reseller charges its own customers, and the difference between the two. The platform figures are read live, so they can change without any action by the reseller; if they cannot be read, 0.40 EUR per chat session and 0.30 EUR per voice minute are used. A reseller that has never set its own prices gets the platform prices echoed back with both margins reported as 0. Requires a reseller account key.

200.description: The current price and margin picture.

patch.description: Sets what the reseller charges its own customers per chat session and per voice minute. Both prices are required and must be positive; the pair is then checked against the current platform prices, and a price that does not clear that check is refused with 400 `validation_error` and a single string listing the reasons. A body that fails the schema itself is also refused with 400 `validation_error`, but there `error.message` is the raw array of validation issues rather than a string, so a client should be ready for both shapes. Prices are stored for the reseller, creating the pricing record on first use, and the change is written to the activity log as `pricing_updated`. Reseller keys only.

requestBody.description: The two customer-facing prices, in EUR. Both must be greater than zero.

get.description: Returns four ready-made pricing tiers computed from the current platform prices: break-even, plus 25 percent, plus 50 percent and plus 100 percent. Each tier carries the suggested chat and voice price along with the resulting margin in EUR and in percent. This is a calculation only: nothing is stored, and applying a tier means sending its two prices to PATCH /resellers/pricing. The response is a bare JSON array, not wrapped in a `data` envelope. This route reads no reseller-specific data, but the reseller gate still applies, so an ordinary customer key is refused.

schema.description: Four tiers, from break-even to the widest margin.

tier.description: Name of the tier, for example `Minimal (Break-even)` or `Standard (25% Margin)`.

chatSessionPrice.description: Suggested customer price per chat session, in EUR.

voiceMinutePrice.description: Suggested customer price per voice minute, in EUR.

chatMargin.description: Suggested price minus the platform chat price, in EUR.

voiceMargin.description: Suggested price minus the platform voice price, in EUR.

chatMarginPercent.description: The chat margin as a percentage of the platform price.

voiceMarginPercent.description: The voice margin as a percentage of the platform price.

get.description: Returns the reseller stock of prepaid voice minutes and chat messages, together with the lifetime totals purchased and consumed, the low-balance alert threshold and the timestamps of the last purchase and the last consumption. A reseller that has never held credits gets a synthetic all-zero record with a threshold of 100 and no record identifier instead of a 404. Requires a reseller-linked API key.

Returns the movements on the prepaid credit ledger, newest first. Every purchase and every deduction is recorded, each with the balances that resulted from it, so the ledger can be replayed. Like the activity log this listing is capped and not paginated: `limit` defaults to 50 and is clamped into the range 1 to 200, and there is no way to page further back. Only a reseller key is admitted.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many movements to return, newest first. Clamped into the range 1 to 200; a value that is not a number falls back to 50.

voiceMinutesBalance.description: Voice minute balance after the movement.

chatMessagesBalance.description: Chat message balance after the movement.

paymentId.description: Payment reference of a purchase, where one exists.

get.summary: Check which payment credentials are configured
get.description: A deliberately minimal status check: two booleans saying whether a card processor secret key and whether wallet credentials are stored. No key material, not even a masked or truncated form of it, is ever returned. Use GET /resellers/settings for the same two flags alongside the invoicing profile and the publishable key. Answers 404 when the reseller record cannot be loaded. Reseller keys only.

200.description: Which payment credentials are on file.

stripeConfigured.description: Whether a card processor secret key is stored.

get.description: Returns the logo used in the branded customer portal and the trading name shown next to it. Both come back as null when they were never set. This is the read side of the same stored value that GET /resellers/company reports as `brandLogo`. Answers 404 if the reseller record is missing. The key must belong to a reseller account.

200.description: The brand logo and display name.

logoUrl.description: Location of the portal logo, or null when none is set.

displayName.description: Trading name shown beside the logo, or null.

patch.summary: Set or remove the brand logo
patch.description: Writes the portal logo. The single field is required but nullable: send a location to set the logo, send null to remove it. Nothing is uploaded here, the value is stored as given, so the file has to be hosted somewhere already. The activity log records the change as `logo_updated`. A body that fails validation answers 400 with `error.code` set to `validation_error` and `error.message` carrying the raw list of validation issues as an array of objects, not as a human-readable string. Requires a reseller key.

requestBody.description: Where the logo lives, or null to remove it.

post.description: Adds prepaid voice minutes and chat sessions to the reseller stock and books the purchase on the credit ledger. Both amounts are optional but at least one of them has to be present and non-zero, otherwise the answer is 400 `validation_error`. Both kinds of credit are charged at 0.30 EUR per unit, and the resulting total is returned and stored on the ledger entry. The credit record is created automatically on first purchase; if that fails, the answer is 404 with a note to contact the platform administrator. A successful purchase also clears the low-balance alert flag. The response status is 201. Note that this books the credits immediately and does not run a payment: settlement happens outside this call. A body that fails validation answers 400 with `error.code` set to `validation_error` and `error.message` carrying the raw list of validation issues as an array of objects, not as a human-readable string.

requestBody.description: How many voice minutes and chat sessions to add. Each must be a non-negative whole number, and at least one must be given.

201.description: The credits were booked.

voiceMinutes.description: Voice minutes available after the purchase.

chatSessions.description: Chat sessions available after the purchase.

totalPrice.description: What the purchase cost in EUR, at 0.30 EUR per unit.

post.description: Books consumption against the prepaid stock, for resellers that meter usage in their own system and mirror it here. Both amounts default to 0 and at least one of them must be non-zero. A deduction larger than the available stock is refused with 400 `insufficient_balance` and nothing is written, and voice and chat are checked separately in that order. When no credit record exists at all the answer is 404. The movement is recorded on the ledger, optionally attributed to one of the reseller customers, and the last-usage timestamp is updated. Note that the response reports the chat figure under `chatMessages`, while the purchase endpoint calls the same counter `chatSessions`. A body that fails validation answers 400 with `error.code` set to `validation_error` and `error.message` carrying the raw list of validation issues as an array of objects, not as a human-readable string.

requestBody.description: What to deduct. `customerId` attributes the deduction to one of your customers and `description` overrides the generated ledger note.

voiceMinutes.description: Voice minutes left after the deduction.

chatMessages.description: Chat messages left after the deduction.

post.summary: Import a number the reseller already owns
post.description: Brings a number the reseller holds with its own carrier onto the platform, instead of buying one from the number marketplace. Two provider styles are accepted: a SIP trunk, where the inbound and outbound trunk configuration including registrar credentials is passed in the `sipTrunk` object, and a hosted carrier account, where the account identifier and token are passed in the object named after the second `provider` value. The number is registered with the voice engine first and only then stored locally, booked under the calling reseller with the calling user as owner, so a failure at the engine leaves no local record behind. The response status is 201 and carries both the external and the local identifier. When the platform has no master voice engine credential configured the answer is 412 `precondition_failed`. A body that fails validation answers 400 with `error.code` set to `validation_error` and `error.message` carrying the raw list of validation issues as an array of objects, not as a human-readable string. Requires a reseller-owned API key.

requestBody.description: The number, its label, the direction flags (both default to true) and exactly one provider configuration matching the `provider` field. A provider block that does not match the selected provider is ignored.

201.description: The number was imported.

phoneNumberId.description: Identifier the voice engine assigned to the imported number.

localId.description: Identifier of the stored phone number record, as used by the other reseller phone number endpoints.

412.description: The platform has no voice engine credential configured, so numbers cannot be imported. Contact the platform administrator.

patch.description: Blocks a customer from logging in and from using the API by setting its account state to suspended. The customer must belong to the calling reseller; a customer that does not, or does not exist, answers 404 rather than 403, so the endpoint cannot be used to discover accounts of other resellers. Suspending an already suspended account succeeds and changes nothing. The action is written to the activity log as `customer_suspended`. This endpoint takes no request body. Only reseller keys are accepted.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric user id of the customer to suspend. A non-numeric value answers 400 `invalid_id`.

patch.x-no-request-body: This endpoint takes no request body.

customerId.description: The customer that was acted on.

status.description: The account state after the call.

patch.description: The counterpart of the suspend call: sets the customer account state back to active so login and API access work again. Ownership is checked the same way, so a customer of another reseller answers 404. The call is unconditional, meaning an account that was never suspended is simply set to active. The activity log records it as `customer_unsuspended`. No request body is expected. The API key has to belong to a reseller account.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric user id of the customer to reactivate. A non-numeric value answers 400 `invalid_id`.

patch.x-no-request-body: This endpoint takes no request body.

customerId.description: The customer that was acted on.

status.description: The account state after the call.

get.summary: Get one customer usage broken down by type
get.description: Aggregates one customer consumption over a date window, grouped by usage type, with quantity, revenue, platform cost and margin per type. Types with no consumption in the window do not appear, so the array can be empty. The window is given by `from` and `to` and defaults to the first day of the current month at midnight up to now. Unlike the reseller-wide analytics endpoints, these two values are not validated: an unparseable date is passed to the query as-is and surfaces as 500 `internal_error` rather than as a 400. The customer must belong to the calling reseller, otherwise the answer is 404. The window that was actually applied is echoed back under `period`. Reseller keys only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric user id of the customer. A non-numeric value answers 400 `invalid_id`.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start of the window, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Defaults to the first day of the current month at midnight. Not validated: an unreadable value produces a 500.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End of the window, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Defaults to the moment the request is handled. Not validated: an unreadable value produces a 500.

200.description: The customer consumption in the window.

customerId.description: The customer the figures belong to.

from.description: Start of the window that was applied.

to.description: End of the window that was applied.

usage.description: One row per usage type that saw consumption in the window.

usageType.description: What was consumed, for example `voice_minute` or `chat_session`.

totalRevenue.description: What the customer was charged, in EUR.

totalCost.description: What the platform charged the reseller for it, in EUR.

get.description: Returns the reseller own prepaid EUR balance as a plain figure, with the currency and a preformatted string. This is the same balance that GET /resellers/balance-status reports, without the warning level, and it is kept deliberately small so external billing systems can poll it cheaply. Answers 404 when the reseller record behind the key cannot be found. Not reachable with a non-reseller API key.

balance.description: Current prepaid balance, as a number.

formatted.description: The balance rendered with a euro sign and two decimals.

post.description: Creates an outbound campaign: a named list of up to 10000 numbers that one voice agent will call. The campaign is created in state `draft` and nothing is dialled until you submit it, so this call places no calls and incurs no call charges. The agent must belong to you, and so must `callerPhoneNumberId` if you set one; either being unknown or owned by someone else gives 404. Per-recipient `metadata` is handed to the agent as conversation context, which is how you personalise each call. This operation is guarded by the `write:agents` scope rather than a scope of its own.

requestBody.description: The campaign name, the database id of the voice agent that will place the calls, and the recipient list. Optionally `scheduledTime`, an ISO 8601 timestamp for when calls should begin, and `callerPhoneNumberId`, the database id of the number to call from; without it the system default number is used.

agentId.description: Database ID of the voice agent to use

metadata.description: Custom key-value data passed to the agent as context

scheduledTime.description: ISO 8601 timestamp. If omitted, calls start immediately upon submission.

callerPhoneNumberId.description: Database ID of the phone number to call from. If omitted, system default is used.

201.description: The draft campaign was created.

get.description: Returns the account's outbound campaigns, newest first. Query parameters are validated strictly: an unrecognised `status`, or a `perPage` above 100, is rejected with 400 rather than quietly clamped, which is different from the paging behaviour elsewhere in this API. The `pagination` block echoes the applied page and page size and carries `total`, a real count of the campaigns matching the same `status` filter as the page. Reading campaigns uses the `read:agents` scope rather than a scope of its own.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page to return, starting at 1. Defaults to 1. A value below 1 is rejected with 400, not clamped.

parameters.name: perPage
parameters.description: Items per page, from 1 to 100. Defaults to 20. A value outside that range is rejected with 400, not clamped.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Return only campaigns in this state. Any other value is rejected with 400.

200.description: One page of campaigns, newest first, with the full count in `pagination.total`.

perPage.description: Page size that was applied after clamping.

total.description: Total number of matching records, across all pages.

get.description: Returns one campaign with its current counters: how many numbers it holds and how many calls have succeeded, failed or are still waiting. `batchId` stays null until the campaign is submitted. The counters are the ones stored on the campaign record and are updated as call results arrive, so poll this endpoint to follow a running campaign. It is guarded by the `read:agents` scope rather than a scope of its own.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Identifier of the campaign. A non-numeric value is rejected with 400.

delete.description: Deletes a campaign and its recipient rows permanently. Only a campaign that was never submitted, or one that has since been cancelled or failed, can be deleted: a submitted campaign in any other state is refused with 409 and has to be cancelled first. Deleting removes the recipient history along with the campaign, so export anything you need from the recipients endpoint before calling this. The response is a bare confirmation message with no `success` field, and the operation uses the `write:agents` scope rather than a scope of its own.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Identifier of the campaign.

200.description: The campaign and its recipients were deleted.

message.description: Human-readable confirmation. There is no `success` field on this response.

post.summary: Submit a campaign and start calling
post.description: Hands a draft campaign to the calling infrastructure and starts it. This is the point where calls are actually placed and charged, so treat it as the irreversible step: only a campaign in state `draft` can be submitted, and submitting one in any other state is refused with 409. A campaign whose recipient list turned out to be empty is refused with 400. If the campaign carries a scheduled time it moves to `scheduled` and dialling begins then, otherwise it moves to `pending` and begins immediately; the state may come straight back as `running` or `completed` if dispatch reports that far already. Outbound calling being unconfigured on the platform gives 503, and a dispatch that returned no batch identifier gives 502. This operation uses the `write:agents` scope rather than a scope of its own.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Identifier of the draft campaign to submit.

post.x-no-request-body: This endpoint takes no request body. Everything needed was set when the campaign was created.

batchId.description: Identifier of the dispatched batch. Keep it for support enquiries.

status.description: The state the campaign moved to.

502.description: The campaign was dispatched but the calling infrastructure answered without a batch identifier, so the campaign was left unchanged. Safe to retry.

503.description: Outbound calling is not configured on this platform, so nothing could be dispatched. Contact support rather than retrying.

post.summary: Cancel a running or scheduled campaign
post.description: Stops a submitted campaign: pending calls are abandoned and the campaign moves to `cancelled`. Calls already placed are not undone and remain chargeable, so cancelling limits further spend rather than reversing it. A campaign that was never submitted is refused with 400 and should be deleted instead, and one that is already `completed`, `cancelled` or `failed` is refused with 409. Cancellation is recorded locally even when the upstream stop could not be attempted. This operation uses the `write:agents` scope rather than a scope of its own.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Identifier of the campaign to cancel.

post.x-no-request-body: This endpoint takes no request body.

get.summary: List a campaign's recipients and call results
get.description: Returns the numbers in a campaign together with the outcome of each call: status, duration, cost and the identifier of the conversation it produced, where there is one. Rows come back in storage order, which is the order they were supplied in, and the campaign's own state is repeated in `campaignStatus` so a poller does not need a second request. Paging defaults to 50 per page here rather than 20, and `perPage` is clamped to 100. The `pagination` block carries `total`, a count of the recipients stored for this campaign. This operation uses the `read:agents` scope rather than a scope of its own.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Identifier of the campaign. A non-numeric value is rejected with 400.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page to return. Starts at 1; values below 1 are clamped to 1.

parameters.name: perPage
parameters.description: Items per page. Clamped to the range 1 to 100; larger values are reduced to 100.

200.description: One page of recipients, with the campaign state alongside.

data.description: The recipients on this page, in the order they were supplied.

perPage.description: Page size that was applied after clamping.

total.description: Total number of matching records, across all pages.

campaignStatus.description: Current state of the campaign these recipients belong to.

post.description: Creates a customer account under the calling reseller and returns the credentials an external billing system needs to hand to the end customer. When `planId` is given, the plan must belong to the calling reseller, otherwise the call answers 404; a matching plan is written onto the user and a primary one-month auto-renewing subscription is opened, which is what unlocks access for the new account. A temporary password is always generated and stored hashed, but it is only returned in the response when `sendWelcomeEmail` is true, which is the default; with it set to false the field is absent and the password cannot be recovered afterwards. An email that already exists anywhere on the platform answers 409 `conflict`, and the endpoint is limited to 10 calls per minute per API key, answering 429 `rate_limit_exceeded` beyond that. The whole provisioning router is reserved for API keys issued to a reseller: a key without a reseller behind it is rejected with 403 `forbidden` before the handler runs. No additional scope is checked on this route.

requestBody.description: The customer profile to create. Only `email` is required. The address fields are stored on the billing profile, and `country` is resolved to a two-letter code, staying empty when the text cannot be resolved. `language` sets the interface language of the new account and `planId` must reference a plan owned by the calling reseller.

201.description: The account was created.

userId.description: Identifier of the new account. This is the value to pass back as `serviceId` on every later lifecycle call.

portalUrl.description: Login URL for the customer. Points at the reseller portal when the reseller has a portal slug, otherwise at the platform login.

tempPassword.description: Generated password in clear text, present only when `sendWelcomeEmail` was true. Deliver it to the customer and discard it; it cannot be read again.

post.description: Locks a customer account: the account status becomes `suspended` and any active subscription is paused, so the billing middleware blocks the customer from using the product. Nothing is deleted, agents and data stay in place, and the change is reversible with POST /provisioning/unsuspend. The customer must belong to the calling reseller, otherwise the call answers 404, which is also the answer for an unknown id. Suspending an already suspended account succeeds and changes nothing. The whole provisioning router is reserved for API keys issued to a reseller: a key without a reseller behind it is rejected with 403 `forbidden` before the handler runs. No additional scope is checked on this route.

requestBody.description: Identifies the customer. `serviceId` is the numeric user id returned by POST /provisioning/create, passed as a string; a value that is not numeric answers 400.

post.description: Reverses a suspension: the account status returns to `active` and any subscription left in the paused state is set back to active, restoring the customer access. Only paused subscriptions are touched, so a subscription that was cancelled separately stays cancelled and the customer may still be blocked by billing. The customer must belong to the calling reseller, otherwise the call answers 404. Unsuspending an active account succeeds and changes nothing. The whole provisioning router is reserved for API keys issued to a reseller: a key without a reseller behind it is rejected with 403 `forbidden` before the handler runs. No additional scope is checked on this route.

requestBody.description: Identifies the customer. `serviceId` is the numeric user id, passed as a string; a value that is not numeric answers 400.

post.description: Ends a customer relationship in a data-protection compliant way. This is destructive and cannot be undone: the email is replaced with a generated placeholder, the name and company are cleared, the password and all stored external service credentials are wiped, every voice agent and chatbot is set inactive, and all subscriptions are cancelled with a timestamp. The row itself is kept so the audit trail survives. The stored account status is `suspended`, which is what the response reports in `status`: the account-status field has no `terminated` value to write, so a terminated account is a suspended row whose personal data is gone. The separate `terminated` flag in the response is what distinguishes it from an ordinary suspension. The customer must belong to the calling reseller, otherwise the call answers 404. The whole provisioning router is reserved for API keys issued to a reseller: a key without a reseller behind it is rejected with 403 `forbidden` before the handler runs. No additional scope is checked on this route.

requestBody.description: Identifies the customer. `serviceId` is the numeric user id, passed as a string; a value that is not numeric answers 400.

200.description: The account was terminated and its personal data anonymized. `status` is `suspended`, the value actually stored, and `terminated` is true.

post.summary: Move a customer to another plan
post.description: Upgrades or downgrades a customer to a different billing plan. Both the customer and the target plan must belong to the calling reseller, and either failing that check answers 404 with the same message. The plan is written onto the user record and onto the primary subscription; nothing else about the subscription is changed, so the renewal date, contract duration and status stay as they were, and no proration or invoice is produced by this call. Remaining allowances already granted to the customer are not recalculated here. The whole provisioning router is reserved for API keys issued to a reseller: a key without a reseller behind it is rejected with 403 `forbidden` before the handler runs. No additional scope is checked on this route.

requestBody.description: `serviceId` is the numeric user id passed as a string, and `planId` is the numeric identifier of a plan owned by the calling reseller, as listed by GET /provisioning/plans.

userId.description: The customer account that was moved.

planId.description: The plan the customer is now on.

get.description: Confirms that a reseller API key is wired up correctly and reports what the integration needs to know before it starts provisioning: the reseller record, its status, whether a customer portal slug is configured, the portal login URL, and how many customers are currently linked to the reseller. `portalUrl` is null when no portal slug is set, in which case customers are sent to the platform login instead. The customer count is the total number of linked customers, without regard to their account status, despite the field name. The whole provisioning router is reserved for API keys issued to a reseller: a key without a reseller behind it is rejected with 403 `forbidden` before the handler runs. No additional scope is checked on this route.

200.description: The reseller setup behind the API key.

portalConfigured.description: True when a customer portal slug is set.

portalUrl.description: Customer portal login URL, or null when no portal slug is set.

activeCustomers.description: Number of customers linked to this reseller. Not filtered by account status.

apiVersion.description: Version string reported by the provisioning interface. Fixed at `1.0.0` and independent of the public API version.

get.description: Returns the active billing plans owned by the calling reseller, so an external billing system can map each of its products onto the right `planId` before calling POST /provisioning/create or POST /provisioning/change-package. Inactive plans are excluded and cannot be assigned. The list is ordered by the configured sort order and then by name, is not paginated, and takes no query parameters. The plans are returned under a `plans` key rather than the usual `data` envelope. The whole provisioning router is reserved for API keys issued to a reseller: a key without a reseller behind it is rejected with 403 `forbidden` before the handler runs. No additional scope is checked on this route.

200.description: The active plans of the calling reseller.

plans.description: The active plans, in display order.

type.description: Kind of plan, for example a subscription or a credit package.

priceEur.description: Price in EUR. Returned as stored, which is a decimal string.

billingCycle.description: How often the plan is billed, for example `monthly`.

voiceMinutesPerMonth.description: Monthly voice-minute allowance. Null when unlimited or not set.

chatConversationsPerMonth.description: Monthly chat-conversation allowance. Null when unlimited or not set.

maxAgents.description: Maximum number of agents the plan permits. Null when unlimited or not set.

get.description: Reports that the API process is up and which version of the public interface it serves. This route is mounted before authentication, so it needs no API key and consumes no rate limit budget. The `version` field is the same value the OpenAPI document reports in `info.version`, which makes it the reliable way to tell which build you are talking to. It performs no database or downstream check: a 200 means the HTTP layer answered, not that every dependency is healthy.

status.description: Always `ok` when the request is answered.

version.description: Version of the public API interface, for example `1.6.0`.

timestamp.description: Server time when the probe was answered, in ISO-8601.
